battle.name: 伊納羅斯二世
battle.brief: 公元前460年，薩伊特王朝的伊納羅斯二世舉兵反對波斯王阿爾塔薛西斯二世，雅典派二百艘三列槳艦入尼羅河助戰。波斯軍在拉刻代蒙尼俄斯率領下奪孟斐斯，海軍在三角洲擊潰埃及與雅典聯軍，亞摩斯二世被俘。伊納羅斯退守要塞，最後被交回波斯釘上十字架。卡面亞述長弓，即兩軍弓手所用的角製複合弓。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 伊納羅斯二世之戰是埃及薩伊特王朝與阿契美尼德波斯帝國在尼羅河三角洲的一場戰爭，時間落在公元前460年至前454年之間。波斯一方以國王阿爾塔薛西斯二世為最高權力來源，他並不親征埃及，而是留在亞洲腹地，指派總督（薩特拉普）坐鎮孟斐斯，統轄埃及的稅賦、駐軍與屬地城邑；派到埃及前線的波斯將領是雅典流亡貴族拉刻代蒙尼俄斯，即基蒙之子，另有法爾納刻斯·阿塔巴祖斯之子等將官。波斯軍隊的骨架是波斯與米底的重裝步兵和騎兵，真正讓他們在尼羅河站穩腳跟的卻是混合部隊：呂底亞人與阿里阿里人的雇兵、腓尼基與塞浦路斯的水手，國王埃瓦哥拉斯一世更以塞浦路斯的船隊與錢糧支援孟斐斯。埃及一方是薩伊特王朝的國王伊納羅斯二世，他出自利比亞裔的薩伊特貴族，母系連著王室血脈；手下有孟斐斯與三角洲各城的守軍、尼羅河上的埃及水師，以及以利比亞步兵為主體的野戰軍。外援是雅典民主政體派出的艦隊：二百艘三列槳艦，連同水手、軍官與登陸重裝兵，編制與指揮由五百人議事會決定，戰役爆發時的具體指揮者史無前例地記載模糊；後續再入埃及的五十艘三列槳艦則由基蒙率領。雙方體制的差異很清楚：波斯以常備軍、屬國船隊與自上而下的薩特拉普體系運作，埃及靠的是王室的忠誠與三角洲的地形，雅典帶來了艦隊與遠征的經費，卻沒有為叛軍提供足夠的攻城能力。
countriesEn: The war of Inaros II was a conflict in the Nile delta between the Saite dynasty of Egypt and the Achaemenid Persian empire, falling between 460 and 454 BC. On the Persian side the supreme authority was King Artaxerxes II, who did not campaign in Egypt himself but stayed in the heart of Asia and appointed a satrap to sit at Memphis, governing the taxes, the garrison and the subject towns of Egypt; the Persian commander sent to the Egyptian front was Lacedaemonius, an Athenian aristocrat in exile and the son of Cimon, together with officers such as Pharnaces son of Artabazus. The backbone of the Persian army was Persian and Median heavy infantry and cavalry, but what really kept them standing on the Nile was a mixed force: Lydian and Carian mercenaries, Phoenician and Cypriot sailors, while King Evagoras I of Cyprus backed the Memphis operations with the ships and money of his island. On the Egyptian side stood King Inaros II of the Saite dynasty, who came of the Libyan Saite nobility and was tied to the royal blood through his mother; under him were the garrisons of Memphis and the delta towns, the Egyptian war fleet on the Nile, and a field army whose infantry was chiefly Libyan. The external help came from the Athenian democracy: two hundred triremes with their crews, officers and landing hoplites, a force whose organisation and command were settled by the Council of Five Hundred, while the actual commander in the field when the war opened is remarkably poorly recorded; the fifty triremes that came back to Egypt later were led by Cimon. The difference between the two systems is clear enough. Persia worked through a standing army, subject fleets and a satrapy administered from above; Egypt relied on the loyalty of the royal house and on the terrain of the delta; Athens brought ships and the money of a distant expedition, but did not give the rebels the siege power they needed.
people: 留下姓名的多數來自希臘記錄，其中最關鍵的一個是伊納羅斯二世。希羅多德稱他為利比亞人伊納羅斯、尼科斯之子，修昔底德則直接稱他為埃及人的王伊納羅斯；兩種說法並不矛盾，薩伊特王朝的貴族本來就是從西方來的利比亞人後裔，而伊納羅斯的王室血統來自母系。他起兵時依靠的是三角洲的城邑與薩伊特舊軍，但計畫能否成立，取決於兩個關鍵人物的反應。一個是他的姻親亞摩斯，即法老薩姆提克三世的兒子，後世編年稱亞摩斯二世，擔任埃及水師的統帥；希羅多德與修昔底德都記下亞摩斯在海戰中被俘，正因如此，埃及的艦隊在三角洲一役中失去指揮而崩潰。另一個是波斯方面的拉刻代蒙尼俄斯。他是雅典名門基蒙之子，父死於公元前411年的政變之後，他逃到波斯宮廷為客將，卻在埃及率波斯軍打垮了埃及人與雅典人的聯軍；他的父親基蒙此時正被雅典派回埃及去救援伊納羅斯——父子二人在同一場戰爭裡分屬敵營，成為修昔底德時代最富戲劇性的插曲之一。基蒙的援軍只有五十艘三列槳艦，面對已被波斯控制的尼羅河口與沙洲，無法突破；雅典方面又下令召回，他不從，於是被控通敵而遭放逐，公元前450年的陶片上寫著他的名字。塞浦路斯王埃瓦哥拉斯一世站在波斯一方，以王國的船隊與錢糧支援孟斐斯的戰事。反叛方在希臘城邦一側則是靠雅典的議事院與將軍的說服才取得出兵授權，遠征軍的船團組成人數與後續的指揮官，在史籍中留下的痕跡相當零碎。波斯國王阿爾塔薛西斯二世自始在亞洲腹地發號施令，命令靠薩特拉普與信使傳遞；被圍在要塞裡的伊納羅斯直到最後也沒有等到解圍的援兵。
peopleEn: Most of the names that survive come from the Greek accounts, and the most important of them is Inaros II. Herodotus calls him the Libyan Inaros, son of Nikos, while Thucydides simply calls him Inaros, king of the Egyptians; the two descriptions are not in conflict, since the Saite nobility was itself of Libyan descent from the west, and Inaros's royal blood came through his mother. He rose with the towns of the delta and the old Saite army behind him, but whether his plan could work depended on how two other men responded. One was his kinsman Amasis, the son of the pharaoh Psamtik III, whom the later chronologies call Amasis II, and who commanded the Egyptian fleet; both Herodotus and Thucydides record that Amasis was captured in the naval battle, and it is precisely for that reason that the Egyptian fleet came apart in the delta once it had lost its commander. The other was Lacedaemonius on the Persian side. He was the son of the great Athenian house of Cimon; his father was killed in the coup of 411 BC, and he took refuge at the Persian court, where he ended up leading Persian troops in Egypt against the allied Egyptian and Athenian forces, while his own father Cimon was being sent by Athens to rescue Inaros. Father and son on opposite sides of the same war is one of the most dramatic interludes in the age of Thucydides. Cimon's relief force amounted to fifty triremes, which could not break through the Nile mouth and its shoals once the Persians held them; Athens then ordered him home, he disobeyed, and he was charged with treason and exiled, and the name of Cimon is written on an ostrakon of 450 BC. King Evagoras I of Cyprus stood on the Persian side, supporting the operations at Memphis with the ships and the money of his kingdom. On the rebel side in the Greek cities, the authorisation to send the expedition was won by argument in the Athenian council and by the generals; the muster of the ship crews and the later commanders left only a very scattered trace in the sources. King Artaxerxes II gave his orders from the heart of Asia all through, and they travelled by satrap and by courier; Inaros, shut up in his fortress, was never relieved.
kits: 卡面這把亞述長弓，是亞述王國在公元前九至前七世紀用來配合車兵與鐵制兵器的標準長射程武器：木製弓臂外貼牛角，張開時弓身折出尖角，正是所謂的亞述式複合弓。亞述尼尼微王宮的浮雕，亞述巴尼拔王狩獵與攻城圖裡的弓兵，用的就是這個形制；卡面題字所說弓兵在車上射、車兵靠弓兵開路，講的正是亞述人靠弓與鐵的組合征服兩河流域的兵法。這個形制在亞述覆亡之後並沒有消失，而是被波斯人接手並推到極致：《歷史》第七卷描述薛西斯大軍的編制時，弓手一列所用的便是亞述式的角弓；波斯波利斯阿帕達納浮雕上持弓的侍從，以及蘇薩王宮約公元前510年的一道釉面磚弓箭手飾帶，弓手手裡的也都是這種折角複合弓。戰役本身發生在公元前460年，亞述已亡國近兩百年，但亞述式角弓正是當時波斯軍與埃及軍所用的制式弓。埃及薩伊特王朝的野戰軍以利比亞步兵為主，步兵持矛，盾用蒙皮圓盾，盾心有金屬凸起；弓兵持角製複合弓，與波斯弓兵同源。希臘方面，雅典遠征軍是由水手與登陸兵組成的艦隊步兵，隨身武器以標槍、短劍與輕型弓為主，並沒有亞述式的重弓，因此在三角洲的野戰與攻城裡，射擊的質量差距明顯偏向波斯與埃及一方。艦船是這場戰爭真正的主體：雅典的二百艘三列槳艦吃水深、撞角重，適合開放海面作戰，而波斯一方的腓尼基、塞浦路斯與呂底亞船隻數量更多、船身更寬，適合在尼羅河汊口與淺灘纏鬥。攻城裝備方面，古代的攻城塔與投石機在三角洲的濕地不合用，實際靠的是圍城、斷水、塹壕與土壘；運輸則靠尼羅河本身的河運與沿岸驛道，雅典船隊橫渡地中海的糧秣是整場遠征中最吃緊的一項。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card was the standard long-range weapon with which the Assyrian kingdom combined chariots and iron weapons between the ninth and the seventh centuries BC: a wooden core faced with horn, which when braced throws the limb into a sharp angular curve. This is precisely the Assyrian composite bow. The archers in the relief panels of the Assyrian palace at Nineveh, in the hunting and siege scenes of Ashurbanipal, carry bows of exactly this type; the line on the card, that the archers shot from their chariots and the chariots followed the archers in, describes precisely the way the Assyrians conquered the two river valleys with the combination of the bow and iron. The form did not vanish with the fall of Assyria; it was taken over by the Persians and carried to its extreme. In the seventh book of the Histories, the description of the army of Xerxes gives the rank of archers as armed with bows of the Assyrian pattern; the bowmen on the Apadana reliefs at Persepolis, and the archers of the glazed-brick frieze from the royal palace at Susa of about 510 BC, hold this same angular composite bow. The battle itself was fought in 460 BC, nearly two centuries after Assyria had gone under, but the Assyrian-type composite bow was the standard bow of the Persian and Egyptian armies at that moment. The field army of the Saite dynasty in Egypt was chiefly Libyan infantry: the foot carried spears and hide-covered round shields with a metal boss, and the archers carried composite bows of horn, of the same family as those of the Persians. On the Greek side the Athenian expedition consisted of marines and landing troops whose personal weapons were javelins, short swords and light bows; they had no heavy Assyrian bow, and in the open fighting and sieges of the delta the difference in quality of shooting plainly favoured the Persian and Egyptian side. The ships are the real substance of this war: the two hundred Athenian triremes drew deep and carried heavy rams, which suits open water, while the Persian fleet of Phoenician, Cypriot and Lydian vessels was larger in number and broader in the beam, which suits close fighting in the branches and shallows of the Nile. As for siege equipment, the towers and stone-throwers of the ancient world do not work in the wetlands of the delta, and what was actually used was investment, cutting of the water, ditches and earthen ramparts. Transport ran on the river itself and on the tracks along its banks, and the grain for the Athenian crossing of the Mediterranean was the tightest single item in the whole expedition.
tactics: 戰爭可以分成三個階段，每一階段的戰術都因地形而異。第一階段是奪取孟斐斯：波斯軍沿尼羅河西岸的驛道南下，攻城在三角洲上游的孟斐斯，這是埃及的舊都，也是阿契美尼德埃及的總督駐地。孟斐斯一失，尼羅河上游的稅糧、尼羅河的航行權與三角洲各城都落到波斯手裡，伊納羅斯的叛軍被壓回三角洲的沼澤地帶，再無向內伸展的餘地。第二階段是河口封鎖與海戰：波斯水師在三角洲外海與尼羅河各汊口攔截，阻止雅典援軍與上埃及的援兵順流而下；雅典的二百艘三列槳艦與埃及水師在河口外海接戰，埃及水師的船型與船員訓練皆遜於雅典，又在淺水與沙洲之間失去機動餘地，隨即崩潰，亞摩斯二世被俘。弓兵在此扮演的是壓制的角色：兩軍都有成列的弓手在後陣射擊騷擾，掩護己方船隻接近，角製複合弓的射程使弓陣可以在接戰之前先削弱敵方船上的射手。第三階段是圍城：波斯軍包圍伊納羅斯退守的要塞，掘壕、築壘、封鎖周邊水道與運河，弓手居高臨下覆蓋壕溝與接近道路，車隊與重裝步兵在弓幕掩護下填塞壕溝、逼近城牆；守軍以反擊出擊消耗圍城者，但被圍的形勢使每一次出擊都要付出重大代價。希羅多德記錄的結局是慘烈的，要塞淪陷後殘存的守軍死於缺水。雅典方面的戰術錯誤同樣明顯，遠征軍只顧在叛軍一側作戰，既沒有占據孟斐斯以切斷波斯的補給，也沒有在上埃及取得糧源；公元前451年基蒙再以五十艘三列槳艦入尼羅河時，河口與沙洲已在波斯控制之下，艦隊既不能送兵上岸，也沒有突破的空間。
tacticsEn: The war can be divided into three stages, and the tactics of each are dictated by the terrain. The first stage is the taking of Memphis: the Persian army came down the track along the west bank of the Nile and besieged Memphis, upstream in the delta, the old capital of Egypt and the seat of the Achaemenid satrap. Once Memphis fell, the taxes of the upper Nile, the navigation of the river and the towns of the delta were all in Persian hands, and Inaros's rebels were pushed back into the marshes of the delta with no room left to expand inland. The second stage is the blockade of the river mouth and the naval battle: the Persian fleet intercepted in the offshore waters of the delta and at the branches of the Nile to stop Athenian reinforcements and any help from Upper Egypt from coming down the river. The two hundred Athenian triremes and the Egyptian fleet met in the sea outside the mouth of the Nile; the Egyptian ships were inferior in type and in the training of their crews, and they lost their room to manoeuvre in shallow water and among the shoals, and the line broke, with Amasis II taken prisoner. The archers had a suppressive part to play here: both sides had formed ranks of archers shooting and harassing from the rear to cover the approach of their own ships, and the range of the composite bow allowed the archers to weaken the enemy shooters on board before contact. The third stage is the siege: the Persian army invested the fortress to which Inaros had withdrawn, cutting ditches, raising earthen works and closing the canals and waterways around it; the archers covered the ditch and the approaches from above, and the carts and heavy infantry filled the ditch and closed on the wall under the screen of the arrows. The defenders spent themselves in sorties against the besiegers, but the condition of being besieged made every sortie cost dearly. The end Herodotus records was cruel: after the fortress fell, the survivors died of thirst. The tactical errors of the Athenians were just as clear. Their expedition did nothing but fight on the side of the rebels; it did not seize Memphis to cut the Persian supplies, and it did not go upriver to secure a supply of grain. When Cimon came back to the Nile with fifty triremes in 451 BC, the mouth of the river and its shoals were already in Persian hands, and the fleet could neither put a man ashore nor find a gap to force.
data: 可核對的數字不多，而且分佈很不平均。第一類是兩希臘史家的記載。雅典遠征艦隊的規模是二百艘三列槳艦，修昔底德《伯羅奔尼撒戰爭史》第一卷128節與希羅多德《歷史》第四卷167節都記下這個數字；基蒙後一次出動的船隊是五十艘三列槳艦，見於埃庇達洛多斯《歷史文庫》第十一卷62節。戰爭年表：起於公元前460年，陷落通常繫於前454年，也有前455年的說法，從起兵到要塞淪陷，前後約六年。波斯方面的部隊數字不見於上述記載，兩位史家都只寫了大軍而沒有留下編制數字；後人常拿希羅多德記薛西斯公元前480年大軍的表格作為對照，但那是一個世紀之後、規模完全不同的全國動員，不宜直接套到埃及前線。地理距離可以估算：孟斐斯到尼羅河口的佩魯修斯約兩百公里，雅典到尼羅河口的航程超過兩千公里，這就是為什麼遠征艦隊必須依賴沿途的希臘港市補給，也解釋了為什麼遠征的成敗取決於海路而非陸路。第二類是考古與器物資料：埃及晚期的角製複合弓出土數量稀少，多數出自東三角洲的堡壘遺址，保存條件遠不如埃及中部墓葬的漆器與金屬器。第三類是只能推估的部分：伊納羅斯叛軍的具體人數、孟斐斯守軍的編制與要塞守軍的規模都無從查證；可以確定的只有行政層面的事實，孟斐斯是埃及的稅賦中心與總督駐地，波斯王朝在埃及的駐軍是常備的混合部隊，而不是臨時徵發的民兵。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, and they are very unevenly distributed. The first class is what the two Greek historians say. The size of the Athenian expedition is two hundred triremes, given by both Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War, book 1 section 128, and Herodotus, Histories, book 4 section 167. The fleet Cimon brought out later was fifty triremes, which appears in Diodorus Siculus, Library of History, book 11 section 62. The chronology: the revolt began in 460 BC, and the fall of the fortress is usually placed in 454 BC, with some authorities preferring 455; from the rising to the fall of the fortress is about six years. No figure for the Persian force appears in those sources; both writers say only that a great army was sent, and give no order of battle. Later writers often set the table Herodotus gives for Xerxes' army of 480 BC beside it, but that is a national mobilisation a century later and of an entirely different scale, and it cannot simply be applied to the Egyptian front. Distances can be estimated: from Memphis to the river mouth at Pelusium is about two hundred kilometres, and the sail from Athens to the Nile is more than two thousand kilometres, which is why the expedition had to depend on Greek ports along the way for supply, and why the success or failure of the expedition turned on the sea route rather than the land. The second class is archaeological and artifactual: composite bows of horn from the Late Period in Egypt are rare, and most come from fortress sites in the eastern delta, where the conditions of preservation are far worse than in the painted and metal objects of the Middle Egyptian tombs. The third class can only be estimated. The actual numbers of Inaros's rebel army, the composition of the Memphis garrison and the size of the garrison of the fortress cannot be verified. What can be established is administrative: Memphis was the fiscal centre of Egypt and the seat of the satrap, and the Persian presence in Egypt was a permanent mixed garrison rather than a levy of militia.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最表層是伊納羅斯本人的志願：他出自薩伊特王朝的貴族集團，手上有三角洲的城邑與軍隊，在阿爾塔薛西斯二世即位、波斯加緊對埃及的督管之際起兵，意圖把反波斯與重整埃及的權力攬在一處，恢復薩伊特王朝在阿契美尼德體系之內的實力。中間層是薩伊特王朝在波斯體系中的地位：法老只是總督，薩特拉普徵稅、徵兵、駐軍，尼羅河三角洲的城邑由波斯駐軍與本地守軍共管，祭司與地方貴族對這種安排積怨已久，動一個薩伊特王族成員便能把埃及的軍力與不滿一次集中起來。深層是希臘與埃及之間的相互需要。公元前五世紀上半葉，雅典在德利安同盟戰爭中打得順手，帝國的資源大量用在亞洲戰線，但雅典的糧食極度依賴黑海與地中海的穀物商路，埃及的穀物一直是不在帳上的潛在來源；伊納羅斯需要的則是雅典的艦隊與水手，因為埃及的水師不足以外海作戰，而任何埃及王朝要挑戰波斯，必須先有一支能在地中海站住腳的海軍。兩者因此結合。至於波斯的守方為何能迅速壓制：阿契美尼德帝國有常備的步兵與騎兵、可以徵發的屬國兵與船隊、貫通全境的驛道與信使系統，關鍵的孟斐斯與河口可以同時用兵，而叛軍的背後是沒有海軍、沒有遠征經費的三角洲沼地。
causeEn: There are three layers of cause. The outermost is the ambition of Inaros himself. He came from the noble group of the Saite dynasty, with the towns and the soldiers of the delta in his hand, and he rose at the moment when Artaxerxes II had taken the throne and Persia was tightening its control of Egypt, meaning to gather the cause of revolt against Persia and the business of restoring Egyptian power into one pair of hands, and to recover the real power of the Saite house within the Achaemenid system. The middle layer is the position of the Saite dynasty inside the Persian system. The pharaoh was only a governor; the satrap levied taxes and men and kept garrisons; the towns of the Nile delta were held jointly by a Persian garrison and local defenders; priests and provincial nobles had long been dissatisfied with that arrangement, and moving one member of the Saite royal house could gather the military strength of Egypt and its resentments in a single stroke. The deepest layer is the mutual need of Greece and Egypt. In the first half of the fifth century BC Athens was winning easily in the war of the Delian League, and the empire's resources were being spent heavily on the Asian front, but the grain of Athens depended utterly on the grain routes of the Black Sea and the Mediterranean, and the grain of Egypt had always been a source that did not yet appear in the accounts. What Inaros needed was Athenian ships and Athenian crews, because the Egyptian fleet was not equal to fighting on the open sea, and any Egyptian house that meant to challenge Persia would first have to have a navy able to hold its footing in the Mediterranean. The two therefore came together. As for why the defence could answer so quickly: the Achaemenid empire had a standing infantry and cavalry, subject troops and fleets that could be called up, a track and courier system running the length of the empire; it could put troops into Memphis and the river mouth at the same time, while behind the rebels lay the marshes of the delta, with no navy and no money for a distant expedition.
impact: 對埃及，這場戰爭是薩伊特王朝第一次大規模反波斯行動的失敗。伊納羅斯陣亡後，孟斐斯與三角洲重歸薩特拉普管治，波斯重新確認對埃及的稅賦控制，薩伊特王族則保留王位而成為傀儡；阿姆利希斯在同時期起兵抵抗，一直打到公元前411年才被平定，此後波斯才真正把埃及總督的職位交給自己的心腹。對雅典，遠征的失敗是戰略收縮的起點：一次遠在埃及的敗仗、二百艘三列槳艦的折損與水手的耗損，讓雅典人明白東線的戰爭在沒有埃及的時候拉不長；更直接的是基蒙的政治倒台，公元前450年的陶片放逐把一位屢建戰功的將軍趕下政治舞台，雅典由此把自己的政治危機轉嫁到帝國的戰略上，前449至前448年三十年和平的到來與此不無關係，這場和約的直接原因之一正是東線的僵局。對波斯帝國，埃及保住了，卻也留下了一個不斷發熱的傷口：屬地方面看到帝國並非無懈可擊，敘利亞與巴勒斯坦一線的騷動在同一個十年裡接連出現；同時，塞浦路斯王埃瓦哥拉斯一世在這場戰爭中的效忠，被亞歷山大大帝在三百多年後征服塞浦路斯時拿來當作合法性理由。兵器史上的後果更長：亞述式角弓在波斯、埃及與後來的希臘世界之間流轉，希臘本土的弓兵終於在更輕更長的弓上找回自己的射擊效率，但波斯弓這個名號一直留到羅馬時代，羅馬人寫的戰史仍在抱怨對手的弓比自己的射程遠。
impactEn: For Egypt, this war was the failure of the first large-scale rising of the Saite dynasty against Persia. After the death of Inaros, Memphis and the delta returned to the satrap, Persia confirmed its fiscal grip on Egypt, and the Saite royal house kept its crown as a puppet. Amyrtaeus rose in the same period and was not put down until 411 BC; only afterwards did Persia really entrust the governorship of Egypt to its own creatures. For Athens, the failure of the expedition was the beginning of a strategic contraction: a defeat far away in Egypt, the loss of two hundred triremes and the exhaustion of their crews taught the Athenians that the war in the east could not be stretched out without Egypt. More directly, it was the political downfall of Cimon. The ostracism of 450 BC drove a general of many victories off the stage, and Athens shifted the cost of its own political crisis onto the strategy of the empire; the Thirty Years' Peace of 449/448 BC is not unconnected with this, since one of the direct causes of that settlement was the deadlock in the east. For the Persian empire, Egypt was saved, but a permanent sore was left behind: the subject peoples saw that the empire was not without cracks, and unrest broke out along the Syrian and Palestinian line within the same decade. At the same time, the loyalty of Evagoras I of Cyprus in this war was later used by Alexander the Great, more than three centuries afterwards, as a justification for the conquest of Cyprus. The consequences in the history of weapons run longer still: the Assyrian-type composite bow passed from Persia to Egypt and on through the Greek world; the archers of the Greek mainland eventually recovered their shooting efficiency with a lighter and longer bow, but the name of the Persian bow survived into the Roman period, and Roman historians were still complaining that the enemy bow outranged their own.
result: 公元前460年夏，埃及與雅典的聯合艦隊在尼羅河口外海被擊潰，埃及水師覆沒，亞摩斯二世被俘，雅典的二百艘三列槳艦帶著殘兵退回雅典。伊納羅斯退守三角洲內的一座要塞，波斯軍以大軍圍困並最終攻破，倖存的守軍死於缺水；希羅多德記他最後的結局，埃庇達洛多斯則說他被交給國王阿爾塔薛西斯二世，釘上十字架處死。伊納羅斯二世的名字，就此成為反對波斯而失敗的代名詞，此後的埃及人再沒有以同一種方式反抗，直到三十多年後阿姆利希斯以更隱蔽的方式接棒。雅典方面則是另一種結局，遠征沒有換來任何土地或盟約，只換來一位被自己人放逐的將軍：基蒙於公元前451年再入埃及，五十艘三列槳艦在尼羅河口受阻，雅典又下令召回，他抗命不從，遂於公元前450年遭陶片放逐。戰役的長期結果，是波斯在埃及的統治再延續了近半個世紀，埃及的穀物與地中海航運從此長期在波斯與希臘的角力之下擺動；而在兵器的層面，這場戰爭留下的最實在的東西，是一種弓：亞述式的角製複合弓從兩河流域傳到波斯，傳到埃及的城牆與封鎖線上，再隨著希臘雇傭兵走向西地中海。
resultEn: In the summer of 460 BC the allied fleet of Egypt and Athens was destroyed in the waters outside the mouth of the Nile; the Egyptian fleet was wiped out, Amasis II was taken prisoner, and the two hundred Athenian triremes sailed home with what was left of their crews. Inaros withdrew to a fortress in the delta, where the Persian army invested it and finally took it, and the survivors of the garrison died of thirst; Herodotus records the end he met, and Diodorus says he was handed over to King Artaxerxes II and crucified. The name of Inaros II became a byword for revolt against Persia that failed, and the Egyptians did not rise in the same way again for more than thirty years, until Amyrtaeus took up the cause in a more concealed form. The Athenians got a different ending. The expedition brought back no territory and no alliance, only a general exiled by his own citizens: Cimon returned to Egypt in 451 BC with fifty triremes, was blocked at the mouth of the Nile, was ordered home by Athens and disobeyed, and was ostracised in 450 BC. In the long run Persian rule in Egypt continued for close on half a century, and the grain of Egypt and the carrying trade of the Mediterranean swung for centuries between Persia and Greece. And at the level of weapons, the most solid thing this war left behind was a bow: the Assyrian-type composite bow passed from Mesopotamia to Persia, stood on the walls and the blockade lines of Egypt, and then travelled west into the Mediterranean in the hands of Greek mercenaries.
